Delivery is attorney-mediated. The packet is prepared for retained counsel, appointed counsel or the public defender to file during the disposition hearing. This config produces the document; it does not assert that LegalEase files, appears, or serves.

mechanism: Arrests or charges not initiated by arrest resulting in acquittal or dismissal with prejudice on or after January 1, 2018 may be sealed immediately. The petition must be filed with the circuit clerk on the same day and during the same hearing in which the case is disposed, and the presiding trial judge rules during that hearing. Section 5.2(g)(5)(A) frames the filing as made by the defendant's attorney on the defendant's behalf.

venue.statement: The courtroom in which the case is disposed. The petition is filed with the circuit clerk during that hearing.

venue.note: No county, no circuit, no courtroom, no clerk address and no judge name is prefilled. primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Immediate sealing. Arrests or charges not initiated by arrest resulting in acquittal or dismissal with prejudice on or after January 1, 2018 may be sealed immediately, on a petition filed with the circuit clerk on the same day and during the same hearing in which the case is disposed.

Frames the filing as made by the defendant's attorney on the defendant's behalf: "the defendant's attorney may immediately petition the court, on behalf of the defendant." This is the provision that makes the route attorney-mediated.
Minor traffic offenses. Recorded on this track as an exclusion from the subsection.

Ordinary sealing of non-convictions, available at any time. Not the authority for this petition. Recorded as the fallback that remains open if the immediate-sealing window is missed, and routed through track il-seal-nonconv.

That the court immediately seal the records of the arrest or charge identified in the petition under § 5.2(g). No agency list and no scope beyond that is asserted, because none is stated for § 5.2(g) in any source read.

Two blocks, both left unsigned. (1) The participant's verification signature. (2) Counsel's signature block — counsel's review, adoption and signature is a required manual completion item, because § 5.2(g)(5)(A) frames the petition as filed by the defendant's attorney. LegalEase drafts it; counsel decides whether to file it. No attorney name, ARDC number, firm or address is prefilled; no source supplies any.

provenance.statePackNote: The committed Illinois state pack carries pathway, remedy, fee, safety, required-field, court-routing and filing-instruction data for the statewide § 5.2(d) expungement/sealing suite plus the Nationwide official-form inventory. It records nothing about § 5.2(g) immediate sealing specifically. Track prose, authority, rules, packet composition, exclusions and manual completion items come from the pinned registry entry. The state pack supplies the court name, the fee-variability posture, the sealing-versus-expungement vocabulary rule, the fee-waiver surfacing rule, the RAP-sheet step and the no-invented-addresses posture.
provenance.profileCoverageNote: The compiled IL profile records no pathway, question, ordered decision rule, waiting-period rule, exclusion rule or packet-generator entry for il-immediate-seal. Its nine pathways are adult non-conviction expungement, expungement after supervision or qualified probation, adult conviction sealing, cannabis, human-trafficking survivor, felony prostitution, criminal identity theft, juvenile, and Clean Slate automatic sealing. A full-value scan for "5.2(g)", "5.2(c)(3)(A)" and "certificate of eligibility" returns zero hits; the eighteen hits for "immediate seal" all belong to the § 5.2(h) human-trafficking survivor route, which is a different track. The profile is used here only for the illustrative caption (sourceSections[25]), the terminology and copy guardrails, the fee and filing narrative, and the statewide-forms mandate recorded as a source conflict.
